problem: The vector $a$ has magnitude $3$, the vector $b$ has magnitude $15,$ the angle between $a$ and $b$ is ${40}^{∘}$ and $n$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $a\times b.$ Find $a\times b$ in terms of $n.$ Round your final answer to one decimal place where appropriate.

feedback.problem: The vector $u$ has magnitude $5$, the vector $v$ has magnitude $4,$ the angle between $u$ and $v$ is ${160}^{∘}$ and $n$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $u\times v.$ Find $u\times v$ in terms of $n.$ Round your final answer to one decimal place where appropriate.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\times v & =|u|\cdot |v|\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot n \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{160}^{∘}\cdot n \\  & =20\cdot (0.342\,02…)\cdot n \\  & =(6.840\,40…)\cdot n \\  & ≈6.8n.\end{aligned}
$$
